en.name: Winifred of Wales
en.summary: Seventh-century Welsh noblewoman said to have been miraculously restored to life after martyrdom, at the site of a healing spring still visited today.
en.body: Winifred was, according to a well-established Welsh tradition, a noblewoman who had consecrated her virginity to God and was pursued by a local prince whose advances she refused; enraged at her rejection, he struck off her head, and at the spot where it fell a spring of water immediately burst from the ground, which became known as Holywell and remains a site of pilgrimage in Wales to this day. Her uncle, Saint Beuno, is said to have restored her head to her body and revived her through prayer, after which she lived for many more years as a nun, eventually becoming abbess of a convent, while her attacker reportedly died on the spot, swallowed into the earth. Holywell's waters have been associated with reported healings for well over a thousand years, making it one of the longest continuously visited pilgrimage sites in Britain, having survived even the upheavals of the Reformation. She died around 660, and her cult remains one of the most enduring in Welsh Christian history.
